# 12-Week Cycle-Phased Strength Programme

**Client snapshot:** 28F, recreational lifter, severe primary dysmenorrhea. GP-cleared with restrictions on flow days (1–3 of menses): no high intensity, no heavy Valsalva (i.e., no maximal breath-holding under load — keep RPE ≤6 and avoid loaded compounds above ~70% 1RM), no jumping/impact.

**Programme start:** Mon 1 June 2026

## Cycle Mapping (28-day, last period 1 May 2026)

| Cycle | Flow Days (Mon–Wed) | Follicular (Thu wk of flow → mid-cycle) | Ovulatory window | Luteal | Pre-menstrual dip |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cycle 1 | **Fri 29 May – Sun 31 May** (just before programme start) | Mon 1 Jun – Fri 12 Jun | Sat 13 – Tue 16 Jun | Wed 17 – Wed 24 Jun | Thu 25 – Fri 26 Jun |
| Cycle 2 | **Sat 27 – Mon 29 Jun** | Tue 30 Jun – Fri 10 Jul | Sat 11 – Tue 14 Jul | Wed 15 – Wed 22 Jul | Thu 23 – Fri 24 Jul |
| Cycle 3 | **Sat 25 – Mon 27 Jul** | Tue 28 Jul – Fri 7 Aug | Sat 8 – Tue 11 Aug | Wed 12 – Wed 19 Aug | Thu 20 – Fri 21 Aug |
| Cycle 4 | **Sat 22 – Mon 24 Aug** | Tue 25 Aug – Fri 4 Sep (programme ends Sun 23 Aug) | — | — | — |

Programme runs **1 June – 23 August 2026** (12 weeks). She'll hit **3 full flow windows** during the block (29–31 May overlaps wk 1 start, then late June, late July, late August).

---

## Phase Structure

**Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Reacquaint & Build Base** — full-body 3x/week, RPE 6–7, hypertrophy bias (8–12 reps), focus on technique and establishing cycle-aware autoregulation.

**Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength Accumulation** — upper/lower split 4x/week in follicular/ovulatory weeks, RPE 7–8.5, intensification on compounds (4–6 reps), accessory hypertrophy maintained.

**Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Peak & Consolidate** — top sets at RPE 8–9 in follicular phase, taper accessories, end the block with PR opportunities in week 11's follicular peak.

**Cycle-phase modulation rules (apply across all phases):**

- **Flow days (D1–3):** Mobility, walking, light technique work, banded movements, Zone 2 cardio ≤60% HRmax. No jumping, no maximal lifts, no breath-holding.
- **Late flow / early follicular:** Ramp back to full programming over 2 sessions.
- **Follicular → ovulation:** Best window for PRs, top sets, heavy compounds.
- **Luteal:** Maintain volume, drop intensity ~5–10%, expect higher RPE for same load. Watch thermoregulation.
- **Pre-menstrual (last 2 days):** Deload-style session — lighter loads, more accessory, no PR attempts.

---

## Week-by-Week

### Phase 1: Base (Weeks 1–4)

**Week 1 (Mon 1 Jun – Sun 7 Jun)** — Client just finished flow (29–31 May). Early follicular, energy returning.
- **Mon (Full Body A):** Goblet squat 3x10 @ RPE 6; DB bench 3x10; 1-arm DB row 3x10/side; RDL 3x10; plank 3x40s.
- **Wed (Full Body B):** Trap bar deadlift 3x8 @ RPE 6; incline DB press 3x10; lat pulldown 3x10; walking lunge 2x10/leg; Pallof press 3x10/side.
- **Fri (Full Body C):** Front-foot-elevated split squat 3x8/leg; landmine press 3x10; chest-supported row 3x10; hip thrust 3x10; dead bug 3x10.
- Cardio: 2x 25-min Zone 2 walks.

**Week 2 (Mon 8 – Sun 14 Jun)** — Late follicular into ovulation (ovulation ~Sat 13). Push intensity.
- Same template, add ~2.5–5kg to compounds, sets to 4 on main lift, RPE 7.
- **Optional Sat session:** Light technique + 20-min Zone 2 (low priority).

**Week 3 (Mon 15 – Sun 21 Jun)** — Ovulatory tail → early luteal. Peak strength window early week.
- Mon/Wed: push to RPE 7.5 on squat, bench, deadlift variants. 4x6–8.
- Fri: maintain RPE 7, watch fatigue.

**Week 4 (Mon 22 – Sun 28 Jun)** — **Late luteal → pre-menstrual → flow starts Sat 27 Jun.**
- Mon: full session, RPE 7.
- Wed: reduce volume 20%, RPE 6–7.
- Fri (pre-menstrual): deload — 2 sets per exercise at RPE 5–6, focus on movement quality.
- **Sat 27 – Mon 29 (flow days):** Active recovery only. Daily 20–30 min walk, cat-cow, child's pose, banded glute bridges, diaphragmatic breathing. Heat pad as needed.

### Phase 2: Strength Accumulation (Weeks 5–8)

Shift to U/L split: **Mon Lower, Tue Upper, Thu Lower, Fri Upper.** Saturdays optional Zone 2.

**Week 5 (Mon 30 Jun – Sun 5 Jul)** — Mon is D4 of cycle 2 flow window (flow was Sat–Mon). Treat Mon as a re-entry session.
- **Mon (Re-entry Lower):** Goblet squat 3x8 RPE 6; RDL 3x8 RPE 6; leg press 2x12; calf raise 3x12. No max effort.
- **Tue (Upper):** Bench 4x6 RPE 7; bent row 4x6; OHP 3x8; chin-up 3x AMRAP; curls/triceps 3x10.
- **Thu (Lower):** Back squat 4x6 RPE 7.5; hip thrust 4x8; Bulgarian split squat 3x8/leg; hanging knee raise 3x10.
- **Fri (Upper):** Incline bench 4x6 RPE 7.5; chest-supported row 4x8; lateral raise 3x12; face pull 3x15; tricep pushdown 3x12.

**Week 6 (Mon 6 – Sun 12 Jul)** — Mid/late follicular into ovulation (ovulation ~Sat 11). **Highest output week of phase.**
- All compounds: 5x5 @ RPE 8 on Mon/Tue.
- Thu/Fri: 4x6 @ RPE 7.5, full accessory load.

**Week 7 (Mon 13 – Sun 19 Jul)** — Ovulatory → early luteal.
- Mon (post-ovulation, still strong): test 3RM on back squat or trap-bar DL — top single at RPE 8.5.
- Tue: top set 3RM bench RPE 8.5.
- Thu/Fri: back-off volume, 4x8 @ RPE 7.

**Week 8 (Mon 20 – Sun 26 Jul)** — Late luteal → pre-menstrual → flow starts Sat 25 Jul. **Deload week.**
- All sessions: 60–65% of week 7 working loads, 3x6, RPE 6.
- Thu/Fri: drop one accessory per session.
- **Sat 25 – Mon 27 (flow days):** Active recovery protocol as Week 4.

### Phase 3: Peak & Consolidate (Weeks 9–12)

**Week 9 (Mon 28 Jul – Sun 2 Aug)** — Mon is D4 of cycle 3 flow. Re-entry session.
- **Mon (Re-entry Lower):** Same template as Week 5 Mon, slightly heavier loads if she reports good recovery.
- **Tue (Upper):** 4x5 RPE 7.5 on bench and row.
- **Thu (Lower):** Squat 5x3 @ RPE 7.5; RDL 4x6; accessory as Phase 2.
- **Fri (Upper):** OHP 5x3 RPE 7.5; weighted chin 4x5; accessory.

**Week 10 (Mon 3 – Sun 9 Aug)** — Mid/late follicular, ovulation ~Sat 8. **Heaviest training week.**
- Mon: Back squat 5x3 @ RPE 8.5; RDL 4x5 @ RPE 8.
- Tue: Bench 5x3 @ RPE 8.5; weighted row 4x5.
- Thu: Trap-bar DL 4x3 @ RPE 8; front squat 3x5; hip thrust 3x6.
- Fri: OHP 4x4 @ RPE 8; chin-up weighted 4x4; accessories.

**Week 11 (Mon 10 – Sun 16 Aug)** — Ovulatory window early week. **PR week.**
- **Mon:** Back squat — work to top set of 2 @ RPE 9 (effective PR attempt). Back-off 3x5 @ 80% of top.
- **Tue:** Bench — top set of 2 @ RPE 9. Back-off 3x5.
- **Thu:** Deadlift variant — top single @ RPE 8.5 (conservative, deadlift PRs carry more fatigue cost). Back-off 3x3.
- **Fri:** OHP top set of 3 @ RPE 8.5; weighted chin top set of 3; light accessories.
- Sleep, fueling, and stress management this week are priority — brief her in advance.

**Week 12 (Mon 17 – Sun 23 Aug)** — Late luteal → pre-menstrual; flow expected ~Sat 22. **Consolidation/taper.**
- Mon: Squat 3x5 @ 75% of Week 11 top — feel good, leave reps in tank.
- Tue: Bench 3x5 @ 75%; light row work.
- Thu: Optional light lower (RDL 3x8, hip thrust 3x10, accessories) OR rest if pre-menstrual symptoms strong.
- Fri: Light upper, RPE 6, total session ≤45 min.
- **Sat 22 – Mon 24 (flow):** Active recovery to close block. Debrief Tuesday Wk 13.

---

## Cross-Cutting Notes

**Autoregulation on flow days:** If symptoms are milder than baseline a given month and she wants to lift, allow light upper-body accessory work (rows, pulldowns, curls, triceps, lateral raises) seated/supported, RPE ≤6, no breath-hold. Skip if cramping, nausea, or heavy bleeding.

**Recovery during flow window:**
- Heat application to lower abdomen/lower back
- Diaphragmatic breathing 5 min daily (also reduces pelvic floor tension)
- Magnesium glycinate 200–300mg evenings (if GP supports — confirm)
- Sleep priority: aim 8+ hrs on flow days
- Light walking 20–30 min daily — improves symptoms via circulation

**Nutrition pointers (general — refer to RD for individualised plan):**
- Iron-rich foods in week following flow (red meat, lentils, leafy greens with vit C source) to replenish.
- Don't under-eat in luteal — BMR rises ~5–10%, and undereating worsens PMS and next cycle's flow symptoms.
- Hydration: +500ml on flow days.
- Adequate protein year-round (1.6–2.0 g/kg).

**Tracking:**
- Log RPE, sleep score, cycle day, and symptom severity (0–10) every session.
- After 2 cycles you'll have a personalised picture of where her *actual* output dips vs. the generic luteal-dip assumption. Adjust Phase 3 accordingly.

**Red flags — pause and refer back to GP:**
- Flow significantly heavier or longer than baseline
- New pain pattern (especially mid-cycle or persistent)
- Symptoms not improving despite restrictions — possible secondary cause (endometriosis screening warranted)

Let me know if you want me to write up the flow-day mobility/breathing session in detail, or build out a Phase 4 continuation for September.

# Cycle-Phased Nutrition Plan

**Scope:** General nutrition guidance to support training output, reduce dysmenorrhea symptom severity, and manage cycle-related fatigue. **Not a substitute for a Registered Dietitian** — particularly for supplement dosing, iron status, and any GI/endocrine concerns. Confirm supplement use with her GP, especially given her dysmenorrhea may involve NSAID use (some supplements interact).

Assume a starting estimate of ~2,100–2,300 kcal/day for a 28F recreational lifter at moderate activity — adjust to her bodyweight, goals, and hunger cues over the first 2–3 weeks.

---

## Foundational Targets (Daily, Year-Round)

| Macro/Micro | Target | Why it matters here |
|---|---|---|
| Protein | 1.6–2.0 g/kg bodyweight | Training recovery; satiety in luteal phase |
| Carbs | 4–6 g/kg on training days | Glycogen for lifting; mood/serotonin support |
| Fat | 0.8–1.0 g/kg, min 20% kcal | Hormone synthesis — chronically low fat worsens cycle symptoms |
| Fibre | 25–30 g | Estrogen clearance via gut; reduces cramping severity over time |
| Water | 35 ml/kg + 500–750 ml per training hour | Mild dehydration amplifies cramping |
| Omega-3 (EPA+DHA) | 2–3 g/day from food or fish oil | **Strong evidence for reducing dysmenorrhea pain** — comparable to ibuprofen in some trials |
| Magnesium | 300–360 mg | Smooth muscle relaxation, reduces cramp intensity |
| Vitamin D | Maintain 75–125 nmol/L (test) | Low D associated with worse menstrual pain |
| Iron | 18 mg/day baseline; more if heavy flow | Replenishes losses; prevents fatigue |
| Calcium | 1,000 mg | Combined with mag, reduces PMS severity |
| B-vitamins (esp. B1, B6) | RDA via varied diet | B1 shown to reduce dysmenorrhea pain; B6 helps PMS mood |

---

## Phase-by-Phase Nutrition

### 🩸 Menstrual Phase (Flow Days 1–3)

**Goals:** Reduce inflammation, manage pain, prevent iron deficit, maintain energy for light activity.

**Caloric target:** Maintenance — do NOT under-eat. Appetite may be low day 1; prioritise nutrient density over volume.

**Key foods to emphasise:**
- **Anti-inflammatory:** Fatty fish (salmon, sardines, mackerel) 2–3 servings across these days; extra virgin olive oil; berries; leafy greens; turmeric (with black pepper); ginger.
- **Iron-rich + Vitamin C pairing:** Red meat or liver 1–2x; lentils, chickpeas, tofu, pumpkin seeds, dark chocolate (85%+). Always pair plant iron with vitamin C (peppers, citrus, kiwi, strawberries) to boost absorption 2–3x.
- **Magnesium-dense:** Dark chocolate, pumpkin seeds, almonds, spinach, black beans, avocado.
- **Warm, easy-to-digest:** Soups, stews, oatmeal, bone broth — easier on a crampy gut, and warmth itself eases pain.
- **Complex carbs:** Oats, sweet potato, brown rice — supports serotonin and stable blood sugar (crashes worsen cramps).

**Foods to minimise during flow:**
- Alcohol — worsens cramps, disrupts sleep, depletes B vitamins.
- Excess caffeine (cap at 1 coffee before noon) — vasoconstriction can worsen cramping; also disrupts iron absorption.
- Ultra-processed foods, high added sugar — pro-inflammatory; blood sugar swings amplify symptoms.
- Very salty foods — worsens bloating.
- Raw cold salads if they aggravate cramping — many women tolerate warm meals better on these days.

**Hydration:** +500–750 ml above baseline. Add electrolytes (pinch of salt + squeeze of lemon, or a low-sugar electrolyte mix) — fluid loss + reduced appetite often causes mild dehydration that intensifies pain.

**Targeted supplements (timing matters):**
- **Omega-3:** 2–3 g EPA+DHA — most effective if taken consistently throughout the cycle, but especially important here.
- **Magnesium glycinate:** 300 mg with evening meal — sleep + cramp relief.
- **Ginger:** 750–1,500 mg/day (fresh, tea, or capsules) — multiple RCTs show reduction in menstrual pain comparable to mefenamic acid/ibuprofen.
- **Vitamin B1 (thiamine):** 100 mg — well-evidenced for dysmenorrhea reduction.

**Sample flow-day plate:**
- **Breakfast:** Oats cooked with milk, topped with berries, walnuts, pumpkin seeds, drizzle of honey, cinnamon. Ginger tea.
- **Lunch:** Lentil & spinach soup with a side of wholegrain bread; orange or kiwi for vit C.
- **Snack:** Greek yogurt with dark chocolate squares + almonds.
- **Dinner:** Baked salmon, roasted sweet potato, sautéed kale with garlic and olive oil, lemon.
- **Evening:** Chamomile or ginger tea; small square of dark chocolate.

---

### 🌱 Follicular Phase (Day 4 to ~Day 13)

**Goals:** Replenish iron, support rising training intensity, capitalise on improved insulin sensitivity.

**Caloric target:** Maintenance to slight surplus on heavy training days (+150–250 kcal).

**Strategy:**
- This is the phase to **push carbs** — insulin sensitivity is highest, glycogen replenishes efficiently, she'll tolerate and benefit from a higher carb intake for PR attempts (especially weeks 6, 7, 10, 11).
- Continue iron-rich foods through first week post-flow to replenish.
- Pre-workout: carbs + small protein 60–90 min before lifting (e.g., banana + Greek yogurt, oats + whey).
- Post-workout: 30–40 g protein + 60–80 g carbs within 1–2 hr.

**Key foods:**
- Lean proteins: chicken, fish, eggs, lean beef, tofu, tempeh.
- Higher-carb foods around training: rice, potatoes, pasta, fruit.
- Fermented foods (kefir, sauerkraut, kimchi) — gut health supports estrogen clearance.
- Cruciferous veg (broccoli, cauliflower, Brussels sprouts) daily — supports liver estrogen metabolism.

**Sample follicular training-day plate:**
- **Breakfast:** 3-egg omelette with spinach, tomato, feta; 2 slices wholegrain toast; fruit. Coffee.
- **Pre-workout (60 min before):** Banana + 1 scoop whey or Greek yogurt.
- **Post-workout:** Chicken & rice bowl with mixed veg, avocado, lime.
- **Snack:** Apple + almond butter, or cottage cheese + berries.
- **Dinner:** Lean beef stir-fry, brown rice, broccoli, peppers, sesame oil.

---

### ☀️ Ovulatory Phase (~Day 13–16)

**Goals:** Support peak training output (PR windows in weeks 7 and 11).

**Caloric target:** Maintenance, with full carb refeeding around heavy sessions.

**Strategy:**
- Maintain follicular approach.
- Add antioxidant-rich foods (berries, leafy greens, colourful veg) — slight rise in oxidative stress around ovulation.
- Hydration extra-important; basal body temp rises slightly.
- Don't restrict on PR days — fully fueled lifters lift more.

---

### 🌙 Luteal Phase (~Day 17–28)

**Goals:** Manage rising appetite and cravings constructively, support mood, prep tissues for incoming flow, reduce pre-menstrual symptom severity.

**Caloric target:** **+100–300 kcal above follicular baseline** — BMR genuinely rises 5–10% in luteal phase. Restricting here is one of the most common drivers of binges, poor training, and worsened next-cycle symptoms.

**Strategy:**
- **Stabilise blood sugar:** Eat at regular intervals (every 3–4 hr); always pair carbs with protein and fat. Blood sugar volatility = worse PMS mood and cramping next cycle.
- **Lean into complex carbs at dinner:** Supports serotonin → better sleep, reduced PMS irritability.
- **Increase fibre and cruciferous veg:** Supports estrogen clearance — relevant because dysmenorrhea is often estrogen-prostaglandin driven.

# Cycle-Phased Aerobic Base Programme

**Goal:** Build aerobic base (improved Zone 2 capacity, lower resting HR, better recovery between lifting sets) without compromising strength gains or aggravating dysmenorrhea.

**Approach:** Polarised model — **~80% Zone 2 (easy), ~20% higher intensity** — with all higher-intensity work scheduled in follicular/ovulatory phases and removed entirely on flow days.

## HR Zones (Estimated — Refine with Field Test)

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Z1 Recovery | 50–60% | 96–115 | Very easy | Full conversation, nasal breathing |
| **Z2 Aerobic Base** | **60–70%** | **115–135** | **Easy-steady** | **Full sentences, slightly nasal** |
| Z3 Tempo | 70–80% | 135–154 | Moderate-hard | Short sentences only |
| Z4 Threshold | 80–90% | 154–173 | Hard | Few words |
| Z5 VO2max | 90–100% | 173–192 | Very hard | Single words |

**The bulk of base-building happens in Z2.** Most recreational lifters drift too high — coach her to stay disciplined, even if it feels almost too easy.

### 🌧️ Pre-Menstrual (last 2 days) — Walks Only

**Recommended (low joint stress, easy to control intensity):**

- Resting HR up >5 bpm for 3+ days
- Sleep <7 hr previous night
- Previous lifting session felt notably grindy
- Any flow-window symptoms emerging earlier than expected
- DOMS still significant from Mon Lower

The skip-rule is more important than the protocol. A missed HIIT session costs nothing; a HIIT session done into fatigue can wreck the Thu Lower top set and the following weekend.

- 10 min mobility (hip flexors, T-spine, calves) before leaving session

# On Adding a Plyometric / Power Day

Before I build this out, I want to flag a real concern: **we're now at the limit of what her week can absorb, and plyometrics specifically conflict with her flow-day restrictions in a way HIIT didn't.**

Let me lay this out honestly, then build it if you still want it in.

## The Honest Trade-Off Conversation

Her current week (Phase 2, full follicular):
- 4x intensified lifting (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri)
- 1x HIIT (Wed)
- 1x Z2 base (Sat)
- Daily walking
- 1 rest day (Sun)

Adding a plyo day means **one of these has to give**, or we're stacking a 7th training stressor onto a recreational lifter with primary dysmenorrhea who's already in an intensified strength block. That's not programming, that's wishful thinking.

**Three realistic options:**

1. **Standalone plyo day on Sunday** — She loses her only full rest day. Not recommended.
2. **Plyo bolt-on to existing lifting day** — Most defensible. Add as a 10–15 min primer before Mon or Thu Lower. Trains power, doesn't add a session.
3. **Replace HIIT with plyo day** — Trades metabolic conditioning for power. Defensible if "feeling athletic" matters more than VO2max right now.

**My recommendation: Option 2.** Plyometrics work best as a *primer* before strength work anyway (CNS potentiation), and it solves the recovery math. I'll build that out as the main plan, with Option 3 as a fallback if she really wants a dedicated day.

## Flow-Day Reality Check

This matters more for plyo than anything else we've added: **jumping is explicitly contraindicated by her GP on flow days.** Plyometrics across the cycle will look like:

| Phase | Plyo allowed? |
|---|---|
| Flow days (D1–3) | **No — clinical restriction** |
| Late flow / early follicular (D4–5) | Low-level only (pogo hops, low box step-offs) |
| Mid-follicular → ovulatory | Full programming |
| Early-mid luteal | Full programming, watch fatigue |
| Late luteal / pre-menstrual | Low-amplitude only |

This means in any given 28-day cycle, she has roughly **2–2.5 weeks of full plyo programming** available. Plan around that, not against it.

## Option 2 (Recommended): Plyo Primer Before Lifting

**Slot:** Before Monday Lower (and a lighter version before Thursday Lower in follicular weeks only).

**Why before lifting, not after:**
- Post-activation potentiation — light plyos prime the CNS for heavier strength work
- She's freshest pre-session — best technique, lowest injury risk
- Doesn't add a session or eat into rest days
- Reinforces athletic movement patterns *adjacent to* strength work, where they transfer best

**Structure (10–15 min, before main warm-up):**

### Tier 1 — Low Amplitude / Reactive (always safe outside flow window)
- Pogo hops 3x10
- Ankle hops 3x10
- Line hops (forward-back, side-side) 2x10 each

### Tier 2 — Moderate (follicular and ovulatory only)
- Box jumps (low box 30–45 cm, **step down**, never jump down) 4x3
- Broad jumps 4x3 (focus on stick-landing)
- Lateral bound + stick 3x4/side
- Med ball slam 4x5 (great power expression, no impact)
- Med ball chest pass (against wall) 4x5

### Tier 3 — Higher Amplitude (peak follicular weeks only, Weeks 6, 10 — and only if recovered)
- Depth jump from 30 cm box (step off, land, jump) 3x3
- Single-leg bound 3x4/side
- Hurdle hops (low) 3x5

**Rule:** Quality over quantity. **5 reps max per set on amplitude work.** The moment ground contact time visibly increases or landings get sloppy → stop the exercise. Plyometrics done fatigued aren't plyometrics, they're injury reps.

**She loses her rest day.** This is the cost.

**Saturday Power Session (~40 min):**

**Only run this if:**
- She's hitting 8 hr sleep consistently
- Subjective recovery (1–10) averaging ≥7
- No flow-day symptoms creeping into late luteal

**Skip and replace with Z2 if any:**
- Sleep <7 hr Fri night
- DOMS from Thu still significant
- Any leg soreness or tightness

**Go with Option 2.** It gives her the athletic feel, drives real power development, doesn't compromise strength priority, fits inside her existing week, and respects the flow-day restrictions naturally because plyos sit inside Mon/Thu Lower which already have a flow-day skip protocol.

We've now stacked:
- 4 lifting sessions (intensified)
- 1 HIIT session
- 1–2 Z2 sessions
- Plyometrics as primer
- Daily walking

That's a serious training week for a recreational lifter managing primary dysmenorrhea. **It will work if she sleeps, eats, and tracks symptoms.** It will fall apart if any of those slip.

**Things I'd watch over the next 4 weeks:**
1. Day 1 cramp severity — if it gets worse, total load is too high, full stop.
2. Mon Lower top set quality — if it drops 2 weeks in a row, plyo is eating recovery.
3. Sleep — if she's averaging <7 hr, cut plyo first, then HIIT.
4. Motivation — if she starts dreading sessions, she's overcooked.

**The "more is better" instinct is the most common way good clients stall.** This is a good moment to remind her that the programme is already aggressive, and the athletic feeling she's chasing comes as much from recovery and bar speed on Mondays as it does from adding exercises.

# On Testing a 1RM at End of Phase 3

Short answer: **Yes, with conditions — but not on the date you're probably thinking.**

Let me walk through the timing problem first, because the cycle map makes this decision for us more than the programming does.

## The Date Problem

Phase 3 ends **Sun 23 August 2026.** Looking at her cycle:

| Date | Cycle position | 1RM viable? |
|---|---|---|
| Mon 17 Aug | Late luteal (D22) | No — strength dipping, fatigue rising |
| Tue 18 Aug | Late luteal (D23) | No |
| Wed 19 Aug | Late luteal (D24) | No |
| Thu 20 Aug | Pre-menstrual (D25) | **Absolutely not** |
| Fri 21 Aug | Pre-menstrual (D26) | Absolutely not |
| Sat 22 Aug | **Flow Day 1** | **Clinically contraindicated** |
| Sun 23 Aug | Flow Day 2 | Clinically contraindicated |

**There is no good 1RM testing day in Week 12.** Late luteal/pre-menstrual is the worst possible window for max attempts — strength output dips 5–10%, perceived exertion rises, joint laxity from progesterone shifts is at peak, and she'll be neurologically primed for a sub-par session. Maxing here would underrepresent her actual strength and likely demoralise her.

A true 1RM on Saturday 22 Aug isn't just suboptimal — it's a **direct violation of her GP-cleared restrictions** (no heavy Valsalva, no high intensity on flow days). Not a judgement call.

## Three Viable Options

### Option A (Recommended): Move the 1RM to Week 11

Week 11 is already the PR week of Phase 3, falling in her ovulatory window (ovulation ~Sat 8 Aug). She's at her physiological peak. The original Week 11 plan had her hitting top doubles at RPE 9 — converting one or two of those into true 1RM attempts is the natural progression.

**Revised Week 11 (10–16 Aug) — 1RM Test Week:**

**Mon 10 Aug — Squat 1RM**
- Extended warm-up: empty bar → 40% → 60% → 75% → 85% → 92% → opener 95% → 1RM attempt
- Allow up to 3 attempts at/above 95%
- 3–5 min between top warm-ups, 5–7 min between max attempts
- **Drop back-off sets** — no 3x5 after a 1RM. Done is done.
- **Skip the plyo primer** that day. Save CNS for the bar.

**Tue 11 Aug — Bench 1RM**
- Same ramp protocol
- Spotter mandatory
- Up to 3 attempts at top

**Thu 13 Aug — Deadlift 1RM**
- **Cap attempts at 2** — deadlift 1RMs carry the most recovery cost
- Up to top single at RPE 9.5, not all-out grind
- If first attempt is RPE 8.5, take one more. If it's RPE 9+, stop.

**Fri 14 Aug — Optional light upper**
- Skip if recovery is poor
- 30 min max, RPE 6, accessories only
- Honestly: she should probably rest

**Why this works:**
- Hits the genuine ovulatory peak (best output window)
- Three full days of recovery between maxes
- 7+ days before next flow window — plenty of buffer
- Aligns with her physiology, not against it

### Option B: Test in Week 10, Use Week 11 as Validation

If you want a slightly more conservative approach:

**Week 10 (3–9 Aug):** Test 3RM on squat, bench, deadlift. Use Epley/Brzycki formula to estimate 1RM.
**Week 11:** Original heavy programming as written.
**Week 12:** Taper.

Estimated 1RMs from 3RM are within ~5% of actual for trained lifters. She gets a defensible number without the maximal CNS hit.

**When to use this:** If she's a relatively new max-tester, has never lifted to true failure on these compounds, or you're uncertain about her bar mechanics under maximal load.

### Option C: Move 1RM Testing to a Separate Test Week After the Block

Extend the programme by one week. **Week 13 (24–30 Aug)** lands on flow days early, then recovery. Not viable — same flow-day problem.

**Week 14 (31 Aug – 6 Sep):** Mid-follicular of next cycle. Ovulation lands ~5 Sep.

**Structure of Week 13–14:**
- Week 13: deload week (60% loads, 3x5, RPE 6) — recovery, not training
- Week 14 Mon/Tue/Thu: 1RM testing

**When to use this:** If she's committed to a continuation block in September anyway, or if she wants the cleanest possible test after a true deload. This is technically the textbook approach to 1RM testing — separate test week after a deload.

**Cost:** Adds 2 weeks before she sees her numbers, and pushes into September scheduling.

## My Recommendation

**Option A — Test in Week 11.**

Reasoning:
1. She's in Phase 2 already pushing PRs; her body is calibrated for heavy singles by Week 11.
2. Week 11 sits in her best physiological window of the entire 12-week block.
3. It honours the original programme intent — Week 11 was always the realisation week.
4. Avoids the cycle conflict at the end of Phase 3 entirely.
5. Week 12 then becomes a true taper into the flow window, which is what late luteal should be anyway.

**Then use Week 12 as it's currently written** — consolidation, light, finish the block strong. No testing.

## Conditions That Must Be Met for 1RM Testing

Even with Week 11 timing, **don't test if any of the following:**

| Condition | Why |
|---|---|
| Sleep <7 hr for 2+ nights leading in | Sub-maximal output, higher injury risk |
| HRV down >10% from baseline | Sympathetic dominance, poor max attempts |
| Resting HR up >7 bpm for 3+ days | Incomplete recovery |
| Cycle arrives early (any flow signs by Mon 10 Aug) | Cancel maxes, revert to Week 11 original plan |
| Bar speed on Week 10 top sets noticeably slower than Week 7 | Strength hasn't carried over, test would underperform |
| Any joint niggle or technique breakdown in Week 10 | Wait for Week 14, don't test injured |
| Travel, stress event, or illness in last 7 days | Postpone |

**Cycle-specific risk to watch:** if her cycle shortens slightly (some women have cycles vary 1–3 days), the test week could land closer to flow than planned. Track basal body temp through Week 9–10 to confirm ovulation occurred when expected. If ovulation came early (e.g., Thu 6 Aug instead of Sat 8 Aug), pull tests forward to Mon 10 / Tue 11 / Wed 12 instead of Mon/Tue/Thu, to keep them clear of the luteal slide.

## Technical Requirements for Testing Day

**Non-negotiables:**
- Competent spotters on bench (mandatory) and squat (recommended)
- Safety pins/spotter arms set on squat
- Belt on (she should have trained with one already in Phase 2)
- Full warm-up protocol — no skipping
- Video every top attempt — review for technical breakdown before adding load
- Cap attempts at top weight at 3 (squat/bench), 2 (deadlift)
- **Stop signals:** Hip rise on squat, butt off bench, hitching on deadlift, any pelvic floor discomfort → terminate the attempt regardless of completion

**Pelvic floor consideration:** Heavy 1RM attempts involve significant intra-abdominal pressure. With primary dysmenorrhea, she may not have any pelvic floor dysfunction, but it's worth a brief conversation pre-test: any leakage, heaviness, or discomfort during heavy lifting in Phase 2? If yes, **defer 1RM testing and refer to a pelvic floor physio.** This isn't about her cycle specifically, but max attempts surface dysfunction that sub-maximal training masks.

## Nutrition for Test Week

Layering onto the nutrition plan:

**Sunday 9 Aug:** Higher carb day (~6 g/kg), normal protein, hydrate aggressively.
**Mon 10 Aug morning:** Full breakfast 2–3 hr pre-lift — oats + Greek yogurt + berries + honey + nut butter. Coffee fine.
**Pre-warm-up:** 30 g carbs 45 min before. Banana, rice cake + honey.
**Intra-session:** Sip electrolytes. 20 g carbs (gummies, dextrose) between top warm-up and 1RM attempt is genuinely useful.
**Post-test:** 40 g protein + 80 g carbs within 1 hr.
**Sleep priority:** 8.5+ hr Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed nights.

**Caffeine:** 3–5 mg/kg 45–60 min pre-session is well-supported for max strength. ~200–250 mg for her. Standard cup of coffee. Skip if she's caffeine-sensitive or it disrupts her sleep on test nights.

## What "Success" Looks Like

Frame this with her in advance:

- **Hitting an RPE 9 single at a heavier weight than ever before = success.** That's an effective 1RM whether she had 1 more rep in the tank or not.
- **Grinding a rep at RPE 10 with technical breakdown ≠ success.** That's a number she may not replicate and likely cost recovery.
- **A 5kg PR on each main lift across the block is excellent for a 12-week intensified Phase 2 + tested Phase 3.** Don't frame anything less as a failure.

If she misses a target on test day, the *next* attempt is in Week 14 of a continuation block, not a same-week retry.

## Honest Caveat

She's a recreational lifter who hasn't 1RM-tested with you before (as far as I know). True 1RMs require technical proficiency under maximal load that develops over multiple training cycles. If her Phase 2 top singles in Week 7 looked clean and she handled RPE 9 doubles in Week 11 of the original plan without breakdown, she's ready. If technical quality dropped at high RPE in Phase 2, **use Option B (3RM testing) instead** — it gives her a defensible number, builds toward true 1RM testing in a later block, and lowers injury risk.

### HIIT (Wed, follicular/ovulatory only)
**4 sessions total across the block** (Weeks 2, 3, 6, 10):
- Protocol A: 8x 30s / 30s — VO2max bias
- Protocol B: 4x 4min / 3min — Norwegian, cardiac output
- Protocol C: 2 rounds Tabata — anaerobic, mental toughness
- Default modality: Assault bike or upright stationary bike
- Never in luteal, pre-menstrual, flow, deload, or test weeks

### Plyometrics (Mon primer, Thu in peak follicular weeks)
- **Tier 1:** Pogo hops, ankle hops, line hops — always safe outside flow window
- **Tier 2:** Box jumps (low, step down), broad jumps, lateral bounds, med ball slams — follicular and ovulatory only
- **Tier 3:** Depth jumps (30cm), single-leg bounds, hurdle hops — Week 10 only
- 5 reps max per set on amplitude work — quality over volume
- No plyo on flow days (clinical restriction), pre-menstrual days, or test week

---

## Nutrition Plan Summary

### Foundational Daily Targets
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg
- Carbs: 4–6 g/kg on training days (top end on heavy lifting + HIIT days)
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg minimum (no chronic low-fat — disrupts hormones)
- Fibre: 25–30 g
- Water: 35 ml/kg + 500–750 ml/training hour
- Omega-3 (EPA+DHA): 2–3 g daily — most evidence-based dysmenorrhea intervention

### Cycle-Phased Nutrition

**Flow Days:** Anti-inflammatory emphasis — fatty fish, ginger, turmeric, leafy greens, warm foods, iron + vit C pairings. Add: magnesium glycinate 300 mg evenings, ginger 750–1500 mg, B1 100 mg. Reduce caffeine and alcohol. +500–750 ml hydration. Don't under-eat.

**Follicular:** Push carbs — best insulin sensitivity window. Iron replenishment foods continued through first week post-flow. Pre/post-workout fueling structured. Cruciferous veg daily for estrogen clearance.

**Ovulatory:** Full fueling for peak training. Antioxidant emphasis (berries, colourful veg). Hydration priority.

**Luteal:** +100–300 kcal above follicular baseline (BMR genuinely rises 5–10%). Stabilise blood sugar (regular meals, carbs paired with protein/fat). Complex carbs at dinner for serotonin. Magnesium daily. Reduce sodium last 5–7 days. Taper caffeine.

**Pre-menstrual (3–5 days before flow):** Pre-load anti-inflammatory nutrition. Front-load magnesium and omega-3. Begin reducing alcohol, caffeine, ultra-processed foods. Eat enough — under-eating here drives worse Day 1 cramps.

### Supplements (Confirm with GP)
| Supplement | Dose | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Omega-3 (EPA+DHA) | 2–3 g | Daily |
| Magnesium glycinate | 300 mg | Evenings, daily |
| Vitamin B1 (thiamine) | 100 mg | Daily |
| Vitamin B6 | 50–100 mg | Luteal phase only |
| Ginger | 750–1500 mg | Day 1–3 of flow |
| Vitamin D3 | 1000–2000 IU (test first) | Daily with fat |
| Calcium | 1000 mg/day (food preferred) | Daily |
| Iron | Only if labs indicate — request ferritin test | With vit C |

### Test Week Nutrition (Week 11)
Higher carb Sunday (~6 g/kg). Pre-test meal 2–3 hr out. 30 g carbs 45 min pre-warm-up. Sip electrolytes intra-session. 20 g fast carbs between top warm-up and 1RM attempt. 40 g protein + 80 g carbs within 1 hr post. 8.5+ hr sleep Sun–Wed nights. Caffeine 3–5 mg/kg 45 min pre-session if tolerated.

---

## Recovery & Monitoring

### Daily Tracking Log
- RPE per main lift
- Sleep hours + subjective quality
- Resting HR (morning)
- Cycle day
- Symptom severity (0–10): cramps, fatigue, mood, bloating, cravings
- Bowel regularity (relevant for estrogen clearance)
- Caffeine + alcohol intake

### Weekly Tracking
- Bodyweight (same day, same time)
- Total training volume (sets × reps × load on main lifts)
- HR at standard Z2 pace (should drift down)
- Subjective recovery score (1–10) average

### Back-Off Triggers
| Marker | Action |
|---|---|
| HRV down >10% from baseline for 2+ days | Drop top set RPE by 1, skip back-offs |
| Resting HR up >5 bpm for 3+ days | Replace HIIT with Z2, drop plyo |
| Sleep <7 hr two nights before heavy day | Reduce top set RPE by 0.5 |
| Bar speed notably slower in warm-ups | Cap session at planned top set, no AMRAP |
| Dread before sessions for 2+ days | Force a rest day, reassess |
| Flow-window symptoms emerging early | Pull intensity forward in week, taper into flow |

### Cycle-Specific Watchpoints
1. **Day 1 cramp severity** — if it worsens across cycles, total training load is too high. Cut HIIT first, then plyo, then accessory volume.
2. **Pre-menstrual symptom intensity** — if PMS worsens, hormonal recovery is compromised.
3. **Cycle length** — variation of 1–3 days is normal; track basal body temp from Week 9 to confirm ovulation timing for Week 11 testing.

### Red Flags → Refer to GP
- Flow significantly heavier or longer than baseline
- New pain pattern (mid-cycle, persistent, or different in quality)
- Symptoms not improving despite restrictions — possible secondary cause (endometriosis screening warranted)
- Any pelvic floor symptoms during heavy lifting (leakage, heaviness, discomfort) — refer to pelvic floor physio before 1RM testing

---

## Critical Programme Rules

1. **No lifting on flow Days 1–3.** Clinical, non-negotiable.
2. **No jumping, no Valsalva, no high intensity on flow days.** Clinical, non-negotiable.
3. **Day 1 of any cycle:** Cancel planned session regardless of week, reschedule.
4. **Re-entry sessions (D4–5):** RPE capped at 7, no top sets.
5. **Pre-menstrual top sets:** Triples max, RPE 8 max. No singles/doubles.
6. **1RM testing only in Week 11.** Not at end of Phase 3 — clinically contraindicated and physiologically suboptimal.
7. **Order of cuts if load becomes excessive:** HIIT first → Saturday Z2 → accessory lifting volume → plyo → main lift volume. **Never compromise main compounds before everything else is removed.**

---

## What Success Looks Like at Week 12

**Strength (primary goal):**
- Squat 1RM established, ~5–10 kg improvement on Week 6 5x3 equivalent
- Bench 1RM established, ~2.5–5 kg improvement
- Deadlift 1RM established, conservative top single
- All technique clean under max load

**Conditioning:**
- Resting HR down 3–5 bpm from baseline
- HR at standard Z2 pace down 5–10 bpm
- Demonstrated ability to sustain Z2 60 min comfortably
- Completed 4 HIIT sessions across the block

**Power:**
- Tier 3 plyo executed in Week 10 with clean landings
- Subjective sense of athleticism returned

**Cycle health:**
- 3 cycle data points logged
- Cramp severity ideally trending downward with nutrition + omega-3 + magnesium protocol over 2–3 cycles
- Pre-menstrual symptoms tracked, patterns identified

**Habits:**
- Cycle tracking integrated into training log

# 12-Week Programme Summary: Cycle-Phased Strength + Conditioning

**Client:** 28F, recreational lifter, primary dysmenorrhea (severe D1–3), GP-cleared with restrictions
**Block:** Mon 1 June – Sun 23 August 2026
**Cycle:** 28-day, last period 1 May 2026
**Primary goal:** Strength (intensified Phase 2), with aerobic base, metabolic conditioning, power expression, and nutrition support

---

## Cycle Map Across the Block

| Cycle | Flow Window | Programme Week(s) Affected |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-block | 29–31 May | Week 1 starts in early follicular |
| Cycle 2 | 27–29 Jun | End of Week 4 / start of Week 5 |
| Cycle 3 | 25–27 Jul | End of Week 8 / start of Week 9 |
| Cycle 4 | 22–24 Aug | End of Week 12 |

**Three full flow windows inside the block.** All flow days are active recovery only (Z1 walking, mobility, breathing). All Phase deloads align with pre-menstrual/flow windows.

---

## Programme Architecture

### Phase 1 — Base (Weeks 1–4)
3x/week full-body, hypertrophy bias (8–12 reps), RPE 6–7. Goal: technique, baseline establishment, cycle-aware autoregulation habit-forming.

### Phase 2 — Strength Intensification (Weeks 5–8)
4x/week Upper/Lower split. Compound top sets 3–5 reps, RPE 8–8.5. Genuine PR opportunity Week 7. Intensified at her request after strong Phase 1.

### Phase 3 — Peak & Test (Weeks 9–12)
4x/week U/L split continued. Week 11 = 1RM test week (squat, bench, deadlift) in her ovulatory window. Week 12 = taper to flow.

---

## Cycle-Phase Training Rules (All Phases)

| Phase | Lifting | HIIT | Plyo | Cardio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Flow D1–3 | None (clinical restriction) | None | None | Z1 walks only |
| Early follicular (D4–5) | Re-entry, RPE ≤7 | None | Tier 1 only | Z2 |
| Mid-late follicular | Full programming | Yes (follicular Wed) | Tiers 1–2, Tier 3 in peak weeks | Z2 + Sat options |
| Ovulatory | Peak output / PR window | Yes | Full | Z2 |
| Early-mid luteal | Full volume, intensity -5–10% by RPE | No | Tier 1–2 only | Z2 |
| Late luteal | Reduce volume 20% | No | Tier 1 only | Z2 reduced |
| Pre-menstrual (last 2d) | Deload, RPE 6 | No | None | Z1 walks |

**Rule above all others:** If flow starts unexpectedly during a session → stop session, switch to walk/mobility. Reschedule.

---

## Week-by-Week Snapshot

### Phase 1: Base

**Week 1 (1–7 Jun)** — Early follicular. 3x full-body, RPE 6. No HIIT. No plyo. 2x Z2 (30 min). Daily walks. Establish baseline.

**Week 2 (8–14 Jun)** — Late follicular → ovulation (Sat 13). Add 4th working set. RPE 7. HR field test. Introduce HIIT Protocol A scaled (6 intervals). Introduce Tier 1 plyo Mon.

**Week 3 (15–21 Jun)** — Ovulatory → early luteal. Top sets RPE 7.5. Full HIIT (Protocol A, 8 intervals) Wed. Tier 1 + 1 Tier 2 plyo (med ball slam) Mon.

**Week 4 (22–28 Jun)** — Late luteal → pre-menstrual → flow Sat 27. Deload. Drop HIIT. Tier 1 plyo Mon only. Pre-menstrual deload Fri. Active recovery Sat–Mon.

### Phase 2: Strength Intensification

**Week 5 (30 Jun–5 Jul)** — Re-entry from flow. Mon Lower light (RPE 6). Tue Upper begins intensification (5x4 @ RPE 7.5). Thu first heavy lower (5x4 @ RPE 8). No HIIT. Tier 1 plyo only.

**Week 6 (6–12 Jul)** — Peak follicular, ovulation Sat 11. **Loading peak.** Squat 5x3 @ RPE 8.5, Bench 5x3 @ RPE 8.5, Trap-bar DL 4x3 @ RPE 8.5. HIIT Protocol A Wed. Tier 1 + Tier 2 plyo Mon, Tier 1 Thu. Saturday Z2 (no intervals — protect lifting).

**Week 7 (13–19 Jul)** — Ovulatory tail. **PR Week (Phase 2).** Squat top double @ RPE 9, Bench top double @ RPE 9, Deadlift top single @ RPE 8.5. Back-off sets after. Friday backs off significantly. No HIIT. Tier 1 + Tier 2 plyo Mon only.

**Week 8 (20–26 Jul)** — Late luteal → pre-menstrual → flow Sat 25. **Real deload.** All compounds 60% of Week 6 loads, RPE 6. Drop one accessory per session. No HIIT, no plyo. Active recovery Sat–Mon.

### Phase 3: Peak & Test

**Week 9 (28 Jul–2 Aug)** — Re-entry. Mon light (RPE 6). Tue–Fri rebuild to RPE 7.5. No HIIT, Tier 1 plyo only Mon. 45-min Z2 Wed/Sat.

**Week 10 (3–9 Aug)** — Mid-late follicular, ovulation Sat 8. **Loading peak (slightly reduced from original to preserve Week 11).** Compounds at RPE 8 (was 8.5). No HIIT this week (CNS going into max protocol). Tier 1 plyo Mon only. 40-min Z2 Wed.

**Week 11 (10–16 Aug)** — Ovulatory window. **1RM TEST WEEK.**
- **Mon:** Squat 1RM — extended ramp, up to 3 top attempts at/above 95%, no back-off sets
- **Tue:** Bench 1RM — same protocol, spotter mandatory
- **Thu:** Deadlift 1RM — cap at 2 top attempts, top single RPE 9.5 max (don't grind)
- **Fri:** Optional light upper, RPE 6, 30 min max — or rest
- **No HIIT, no plyometrics this week.** 30-min Z2 Wed, 30-min Z2 Sat. Sunday rest.

**Week 12 (17–23 Aug)** — Late luteal → pre-menstrual → flow Sat 22. **Taper & consolidation.**
- Mon: Squat 3x5 @ 65% of new 1RM
- Tue: Bench 3x5 @ 65% of new 1RM
- Thu: Optional light lower or rest
- Fri: Light upper, RPE 6, ≤45 min
- **Sat 22 – Mon 24 (flow):** Active recovery to close the block.

---

## Weekly Training Template (Phase 2 Follicular Week)

| Day | Session | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| Mon | Plyo primer (Tier 1+2) + Lower lifting | 75 min |
| Tue | Upper lifting | 60 min |
| Wed | HIIT (Protocol A/B/C, rotating) | 25–40 min |
| Thu | Plyo primer (Tier 1) + Lower lifting | 70 min |
| Fri | Upper lifting | 55 min |
| Sat | Z2 cardio (cycle/incline walk) | 45–60 min |
| Sun | Rest / 30-min Z1 walk | 30 min |

**Daily lifestyle walks:** 20–30 min, Z1, every day across the block.

---

## Conditioning Plan Summary

### Aerobic Base (Z2 — 60–70% HRmax, ~115–135 bpm est.)
- 2–3 sessions/week, 30–60 min, cycle or incline walk preferred
- Polarised distribution: ~80% Z2 / ~20% intensity
- Saturday session is anchor — sacrifice Sunday Z2 before Saturday
- HR drift down over block = aerobic adaptation

### HIIT (Wed, follicular/ovulatory only)
**4 sessions total across the block** (Weeks 2, 3, 6, 10):
- Protocol A: 8x 30s / 30s — VO2max bias
- Protocol B: 4x 4min / 3min — Norwegian, cardiac output
- Protocol C: 2 rounds Tabata — anaerobic, mental toughness
- Default modality: Assault bike or upright stationary bike
- Never in luteal, pre-menstrual, flow, deload, or test weeks

### Plyometrics (Mon primer, Thu in peak follicular weeks)
- **Tier 1:** Pogo hops, ankle hops, line hops — always safe outside flow window
- **Tier 2:** Box jumps (low, step down), broad jumps, lateral bounds, med ball slams — follicular and ovulatory only
- **Tier 3:** Depth jumps (30cm), single-leg bounds, hurdle hops — Week 10 only
- 5 reps max per set on amplitude work — quality over volume
- No plyo on flow days (clinical restriction), pre-menstrual days, or test week

---

## Nutrition Plan Summary

### Foundational Daily Targets
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg
- Carbs: 4–6 g/kg on training days (top end on heavy lifting + HIIT days)
- Fat: 0.8–1.0 g/kg minimum (no chronic low-fat — disrupts hormones)
- Fibre: 25–30 g
- Water: 35 ml/kg + 500–750 ml/training hour
- Omega-3 (EPA+DHA): 2–3 g daily — most evidence-based dysmenorrhea intervention

### Cycle-Phased Nutrition

**Flow Days:** Anti-inflammatory emphasis — fatty fish, ginger, turmeric, leafy greens, warm foods, iron + vit C pairings. Add: magnesium glycinate 300 mg evenings, ginger 750–1500 mg, B1 100 mg. Reduce caffeine and alcohol. +500–750 ml hydration. Don't under-eat.

**Follicular:** Push carbs — best insulin sensitivity window. Iron replenishment foods continued through first week post-flow. Pre/post-workout fueling structured. Cruciferous veg daily for estrogen clearance.

**Ovulatory:** Full fueling for peak training. Antioxidant emphasis (berries, colourful veg). Hydration priority.

**Luteal:** +100–300 kcal above follicular baseline (BMR genuinely rises 5–10%). Stabilise blood sugar (regular meals, carbs paired with protein/fat). Complex carbs at dinner for serotonin. Magnesium daily. Reduce sodium last 5–7 days. Taper caffeine.

**Pre-menstrual (3–5 days before flow):** Pre-load anti-inflammatory nutrition. Front-load magnesium and omega-3. Begin reducing alcohol, caffeine, ultra-processed foods. Eat enough — under-eating here drives worse Day 1 cramps.

### Supplements (Confirm with GP)
| Supplement | Dose | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Omega-3 (EPA+DHA) | 2–3 g | Daily |
| Magnesium glycinate | 300 mg | Evenings, daily |
| Vitamin B1 (thiamine) | 100 mg | Daily |
| Vitamin B6 | 50–100 mg | Luteal phase only |
| Ginger | 750–1500 mg | Day 1–3 of flow |
| Vitamin D3 | 1000–2000 IU (test first) | Daily with fat |
| Calcium | 1000 mg/day (food preferred) | Daily |
| Iron | Only if labs indicate — request ferritin test | With vit C |

### Test Week Nutrition (Week 11)
Higher carb Sunday (~6 g/kg). Pre-test meal 2–3 hr out. 30 g carbs 45 min pre-warm-up. Sip electrolytes intra-session. 20 g fast carbs between top warm-up and 1RM attempt. 40 g protein + 80 g carbs within 1 hr post. 8.5+ hr sleep Sun–Wed nights. Caffeine 3–5 mg/kg 45 min pre-session if tolerated.

---

## Recovery & Monitoring

### Daily Tracking Log
- RPE per main lift
- Sleep hours + subjective quality
- Resting HR (morning)
- Cycle day
- Symptom severity (0–10): cramps, fatigue, mood, bloating, cravings
- Bowel regularity (relevant for estrogen clearance)
- Caffeine + alcohol intake

### Weekly Tracking
- Bodyweight (same day, same time)
- Total training volume (sets × reps × load on main lifts)
- HR at standard Z2 pace (should drift down)
- Subjective recovery score (1–10) average

### Back-Off Triggers
| Marker | Action |
|---|---|
| HRV down >10% from baseline for 2+ days | Drop top set RPE by 1, skip back-offs |
| Resting HR up >5 bpm for 3+ days | Replace HIIT with Z2, drop plyo |
| Sleep <7 hr two nights before heavy day | Reduce top set RPE by 0.5 |
| Bar speed notably slower in warm-ups | Cap session at planned top set, no AMRAP |
| Dread before sessions for 2+ days | Force a rest day, reassess |
| Flow-window symptoms emerging early | Pull intensity forward in week, taper into flow |

### Cycle-Specific Watchpoints
1. **Day 1 cramp severity** — if it worsens across cycles, total training load is too high. Cut HIIT first, then plyo, then accessory volume.
2. **Pre-menstrual symptom intensity** — if PMS worsens, hormonal recovery is compromised.
3. **Cycle length** — variation of 1–3 days is normal; track basal body temp from Week 9 to confirm ovulation timing for Week 11 testing.

### Red Flags → Refer to GP
- Flow significantly heavier or longer than baseline
- New pain pattern (mid-cycle, persistent, or different in quality)
- Symptoms not improving despite restrictions — possible secondary cause (endometriosis screening warranted)
- Any pelvic floor symptoms during heavy lifting (leakage, heaviness, discomfort) — refer to pelvic floor physio before 1RM testing

## Critical Programme Rules

1. **No lifting on flow Days 1–3.** Clinical, non-negotiable.
2. **No jumping, no Valsalva, no high intensity on flow days.** Clinical, non-negotiable.
3. **Day 1 of any cycle:** Cancel planned session regardless of week, reschedule.
4. **Re-entry sessions (D4–5):** RPE capped at 7, no top sets.
5. **Pre-menstrual top sets:** Triples max, RPE 8 max. No singles/doubles.
6. **1RM testing only in Week 11.** Not at end of Phase 3 — clinically contraindicated and physiologically suboptimal.
7. **Order of cuts if load becomes excessive:** HIIT first → Saturday Z2 → accessory lifting volume → plyo → main lift volume. **Never compromise main compounds before everything else is removed.**
